about.label: About Me
about.heading: The Creative Mind Behind the Code
about.body: I'm a Product Engineer & Designer based in Buenos Aires, Argentina, building AI-driven products. I combine design and development in a single profile, which means I can take a product from concept to polished interface without losing coherence along the way. I care deeply about the details: the right spacing, the right interaction, the right words. That's how I build digital products that feel as good as they work.

faq.q: Do you work with companies outside Argentina?
faq.a: Yes. I work remotely with clients in the US and Latin America, in English or Spanish, 1–2 hours from US Eastern Time.

faq.q: Can you do only the design, or only the development?
faq.a: Yes. Most clients want both, but I also take design-only or development-only projects.

faq.q: Can you take over an app built with AI tools?
faq.a: Yes. I review the code, fix what's fragile and prepare it for production: data, authentication, performance and deployment.
Write to me with a few lines about your project. I'll reply to set up a 30-minute call.

product-design.title: Web, product & UX/UI design
product-design.tagline: Screens that are ready to build.
product-design.body: Research, user flows, interfaces and design systems in Figma, ready to build.
product-design.metaTitle: Product Designer and Web Designer: UX/UI Design
product-design.metaDescription: Freelance product designer and web designer: research, user flows, UX/UI interfaces and design systems in Figma, designed by someone who also builds them.
intro: Good design solves a problem for the person using it before it looks good. I start with that person: what they're trying to do, where they get stuck, and what the business needs from them.
Because I also write the code, every screen I design is one I know how to build. The Figma file comes with components, states and responsive versions, so development doesn't start with guesses.
includes: Interviews or a review of the data you already have
User flows and information architecture
Wireframes to agree on structure before visuals
High-fidelity interface design for desktop and mobile
A design system with components, tokens and states
A clickable prototype to test with users
fit: You're launching a website, a web app or a mobile app and need it designed
Your product works but people get lost or drop off
Your team has developers and needs a product designer

faq.q: Do you design websites or products?
faq.a: Both. Marketing websites, web apps and mobile apps. The process changes with the project: a website leans on content and brand, a product on flows and states.

faq.q: What do I get at the end?
faq.a: An organized Figma file with every screen, its components and states, and a clickable prototype. If I'm not the one building it, I walk your developers through it.

faq.q: Can you work with my existing brand?
faq.a: Yes. I work inside your brand guidelines, and if they're missing pieces for digital, such as colors for states or a type scale, I propose them.

web-development.title: Web and mobile development
web-development.tagline: Code that loads fast and lasts.
web-development.body: Next.js and React for the web, React Native for mobile, TypeScript throughout.
web-development.metaTitle: Web Developer for Next.js, React and React Native
web-development.metaDescription: Freelance web developer building fast websites and apps with Next.js, React and TypeScript, plus React Native for mobile. Designed and built by one person.
intro: I build websites and apps with Next.js, React and TypeScript, and mobile apps with React Native. The goal is code that loads fast, ranks in search, works for everyone and that another developer can read a year from now.
I can start from a design of mine, from your team's Figma, or from an existing codebase that needs to move forward. Either way you see progress every week in a link you can open, not in a report.
includes: Development in Next.js and TypeScript, or React Native for mobile
A content management system when your team needs to edit the site
Performance and Core Web Vitals checked before launch
Technical SEO: metadata, sitemap, structured data and multiple languages
Accessibility to WCAG AA
Deploy on Vercel or your infrastructure, with previews for every change
fit: You have a design and need a web developer to build it well
Your current site is slow, hard to edit or doesn't show up in search
You need a web and a mobile app that share code

faq.a: It renders pages on the server, so they load fast and search engines read them in full, and it scales from a five-page site to a full product without changing tools.

faq.q: Can you work on an existing codebase?
faq.a: Yes. I start with a review to understand how it's built and what's fragile, then we agree on what to change first.

faq.q: Will I be able to edit the content myself?
faq.a: If you need to, yes. I connect a content management system so your team can change texts, images and posts without touching the code.

ai-features.title: AI features and agents
ai-features.tagline: AI that does a job in your product.
ai-features.body: Assistants, automations and AI features built into your product, with the guardrails production needs.
ai-features.metaTitle: AI Features and Agents Built Into Your Product
ai-features.metaDescription: AI features, assistants and agents designed and built into your web product: search, summaries, automations and chat, with the guardrails production needs.
intro: A model answering in a demo is easy. Making it useful inside a product is the hard part: knowing when it should answer, what data it can see, what it does when it's wrong and how much each answer costs.

I design the feature around the task the person is trying to finish, connect it to your data, and build it with limits, logs and fallbacks so it behaves the same on the thousandth request as on the first.
includes: Finding the tasks where AI saves time, and the ones where it doesn't
Design of the experience: inputs, answers, loading and error states
Integration with Claude, OpenAI or other models through their APIs
Search and answers over your own content and data
Agents and automations that act on your tools
Usage limits, cost tracking and quality checks
fit: You want to add AI to your product but aren't sure where it helps
Your team repeats a task that could be automated
You built a prototype with a model and need it to be reliable

faq.q: Which models do you work with?
faq.a: The one that fits the task. Usually Claude or OpenAI's models, chosen for quality, speed and cost, and built so it can be swapped later.

faq.q: Is my data used to train the model?
faq.a: Not with the business APIs I use: they don't train on your data by default. I also send each request only the data it needs.

faq.q: How do you know the answers are good?
faq.a: We write a set of real examples with the answers we expect and run them on every change, so a new prompt or model can't quietly make things worse.

ai-prototype-to-production.title: From AI prototype to production
ai-prototype-to-production.tagline: From working in the demo to working for everyone.
ai-prototype-to-production.body: An app built with Lovable, v0, Bolt or Cursor that works in a demo but not yet in production: I review it, fix it and get it ready to ship.
ai-prototype-to-production.metaTitle: From AI Prototype to Production: Lovable, v0, Bolt
ai-prototype-to-production.metaDescription: Your app built with Lovable, v0, Bolt or Cursor works in the demo. I review the code, fix security, data and performance, and get it ready to launch.
intro: AI tools make it possible to have a working app in a weekend. What they don't do is check that the database is protected, that a user can't see another's data, or that the app holds up with a hundred people at once.
I start with a code review and a written list of what's at risk, ordered by how much it matters. Then I fix it, keep what already works and leave you with an app you can launch and keep building on.
includes: A code review with a written report of the risks
Security: authentication, permissions and data access rules
Database structure and migrations
Performance and loading times
Error tracking and a proper production deploy
Cleanup so another developer, or the AI, can keep building on it
fit: You built an app with Lovable, v0, Bolt, Replit or Cursor and want to launch it
Your prototype already has users and you're worried about breaking it
Every change the AI makes breaks something else

faq.q: Do you rewrite the app from scratch?
faq.a: Almost never. Most of what the tool generated is usable. I fix what's risky and restructure only what's blocking you.

faq.q: Can I keep using the AI tool after?
faq.a: Yes. I leave the code organized and documented so the tool, or a developer, can keep building without undoing the fixes.

faq.q: What if it's built on Supabase or Firebase?
faq.a: That's the most common case. I review the access rules, which are usually what's missing, and keep the same platform.
